summary: Sugar Grove Knob fire tower, built by the West Virginia Division of Forestry, sold to a private owner and listed on the NHLR register in 2022 as US 1678.

facts.agency: Private owner (formerly West Virginia Division of Forestry)

access.note: The register lists a private owner and gives no visiting arrangement; the tower was sold to the landowner.

events.note: A state report describes a station with a watchman, O.O. Nutter, who stayed at the station at night only in extremely dry weather
A tower at Sugar Grove Knob is connected to National Forest telephone circuits
A 1947 Beckley Post-Herald item, quoted on the forest-lookout site, says O.O. Nutter, retired district forester, is in charge of the fire tower
Registered July 16, 2022 as US 1678, WV 26; nominated by Robert Beanblossom

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Greenbrier County. A West Virginia lookout list and a forest-lookout history site say Nicholas County, and the list's coordinates match the register's point. The sources do not settle the county, so the record keeps Greenbrier, the register's own figure, and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: No construction date found for the current tower; the earliest dated references are a 1916 station with a watchman and a 1926 tower on telephone lines. Staffing is recorded as unknown: the 1947 'in charge' item is not evidence of current staffing. County conflicts (Greenbrier per NHLR; Nicholas per the lookout list and the forest-lookout site). Elevation also differs: NHLR gives 3,112 ft (949 m), while the 1916 report gives 3,158 ft for the station. A Facebook post in search results (WV fire lookouts) asks whether the tower was removed; only its title could be read (login wall), so it is not used. Check status before publishing. Search results also return a different Sugar Grove tower in Berne Township, Fairfield County, Ohio (110 ft, Lancaster Eagle-Gazette, 2017); it is not this tower and must not be merged into this record.
